vocabulary: Semantic fixture notation only, not canonical storage schema, PM node JSON, CM offsets or product API signatures. Source/structured cases deliberately differ.
offset_convention: ASCII offsets in plain text cases are zero-based boundaries; Unicode cases use named whole-grapheme boundaries. Candidate adapters must map safely to engine offsets.
all_cases_inherit: Requirements and invariants in editor-interaction-spec.md; reset fixtures per case, record candidate profile and actual runtime bindings. No automatic acceptance of proposed cases.

FX-TEXT.description: Two plain paragraphs; no formatting, task placement or hidden metadata.

FX-LIST.description: A logical bullet list; IDs below name fixture items, not a required database schema.

FX-TASK.description: Task t1 has one placement in note n1; n2 is empty; inbox exists. Opening a task page is another view of its body.

FX-TABLE.description: Plain 2 by 2 editable table, no merged cells, no header-only restrictions.

FX-MEDIA.description: Source note n1 has plain paragraph p-before, image placement im1, PDF placement pdf1, read-only page embed em1 targeting n2, then p-after. n2 contains Original.

FX-CODE.description: Code block c1, language plain text; line breaks and whitespace are literal.

FX-DATE.description: Paragraph p1 contains Review plus a date mention d1 resolved on insertion to 2026-11-14. No reminder initially.

FX-UNICODE.description: Four independent text fixtures; cursor anchors use named grapheme boundaries rather than assumed engine offsets.

FX-VIEWS.description: Views A/B share logical FX-TEXT at accepted revision r0; contexts ca/cb; selections independent. Window A is focused.

FX-UNKNOWN.description: One opaque unsupported block u1 between plain p1/p2; original payload/asset references retained exactly.

FX-WRAP.description: A paragraph spans at least three measured visual lines. Harness pins font, width, zoom and direction; positions are measured before each movement. Not a fixed engine-specific offset fixture.
FX-WRAP.text: A long paragraph with several words that wraps over multiple visual lines at the fixed harness width.
